sentences.zh: 德宗子德宗皇帝十一子：昭德皇后王氏生順宗皇帝；

translations.literal: The sons of Emperor Dezong—Emperor Dezong had eleven sons: Empress Zhaode, née Wang, bore Emperor Shunzong;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had eleven sons. Empress Zhaode, Lady Wang, bore Emperor Shunzong.

sentences.zh: 舒王誼，昭靖太子之子；

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Yi, son of Crown Prince Zhaojing;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu Yi was the son of Crown Prince Zhaojing.

sentences.zh: 文敬太子，順宗之子；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenjing, son of Shunzong;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenjing was the son of Shunzong.

sentences.zh: 諸妃生通王已下八王，本錄不載母氏。

translations.literal: Various consorts bore the eight princes from Prince of Tong downward; this record does not list their mothers.
translations.idiomatic: The eight princes from Prince of Tong on down were born to various consorts; their mothers are not recorded in this account.

sentences.zh: 舒王誼，本名謨，代宗第三子昭靖太子邈之子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Yi, original name Mo, was the son of Crown Prince Zhaojing Miao, Daizong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu Yi, whose original name was Mo, was the son of Crown Prince Zhaojing (Miao), the third son of Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 以其最幼，德宗憐之，命之為子。

translations.literal: Because he was the youngest, Dezong pitied him and ordered him to be made his son.
translations.idiomatic: As the youngest, he won Dezong's affection, and the emperor adopted him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 大曆十四年六月，封舒王，拜開府儀同三司，與通王、虔王同日封。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Dali, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu, appointed Kaifu Yitong Sansi, enfeoffed the same day as the Princes of Tong and Qian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Dali 14 (779), he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and appointed Grand Preceptor with Honorary Credentials Equal to the Three Excellencies, on the same day as the Princes of Tong and Qian received their titles.

sentences.zh: 仍詔所司，其開府俸料，逐月進內，尋以軍興罷支。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered the relevant offices that his Kaifu salary provisions be delivered monthly to the inner palace; soon, because of military campaigns, payment was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered the relevant offices to deliver his Grand Preceptor stipend to the inner palace each month, but payment was soon suspended when the armies were mobilized.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，領四鎮北庭行軍、涇原節度大使；

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, he took charge of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign army and served as Jiedushi of Jingyuan;
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 1 (780), he assumed command of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign army and served as military governor of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 以涇州刺史孟皞為節度留後。

translations.literal: Meng Hao, prefect of Jingzhou, was made deputy Jiedushi.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hao, the prefect of Jingzhou, was appointed deputy military governor.

sentences.zh: 以誼愛弟之子，諸王之長，軍國大事，欲其更踐，必委試之。

translations.literal: Because Yi was the beloved younger brother's son and the eldest among the princes, whenever there were major military and state affairs, Dezong wished him to gain further experience and invariably entrusted trials to him.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's beloved nephew and the eldest among the princes, Yi was invariably given trial assignments whenever major military or state affairs arose, so that he might gain further experience.

sentences.zh: 明年，尚父郭子儀病篤，上御紫宸，命誼持制書省之。

translations.literal: The next year, the Esteemed Father Guo Ziyi was gravely ill; the emperor went to Zichen Hall and ordered Yi to carry the imperial writ and visit him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Guo Ziyi, the Esteemed Father, lay gravely ill, the emperor went to Zichen Hall and ordered Yi to carry an imperial writ and visit him.

sentences.zh: 誼冠遠遊冠，絳紗袍，乘象輅，駕駟馬，飛龍騎士三百人隨之。

translations.literal: Yi wore the distant-travel cap and crimson gauze robe, rode in an elephant carriage drawn by four horses, and three hundred Feilong cavalry followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wore the distant-travel cap and a crimson gauze robe, rode in an elephant carriage drawn by a team of four, and was escorted by three hundred Feilong cavalry.

sentences.zh: 國府之官，皆褲褶騎而導前，鹵簿備引而不樂，在遏密故也。

translations.literal: The officials of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan all rode ahead in trousers and jackets; the full guard of honor was deployed but without music, because of the period of restrained mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Imperial Clan Directorate all rode ahead in riding dress, and the full guard of honor was deployed without music, in observance of mourning restraint.

sentences.zh: 及門，郭氏子弟迎拜於外，王不答拜。

translations.literal: At the gate, Guo's sons and younger relatives welcomed and bowed outside; the prince did not return the bow.
translations.idiomatic: At the gate, members of the Guo clan came out to welcome him and bowed, but the prince did not return their bows.

sentences.zh: 子儀臥不能興，以手叩頭謝恩已。

translations.literal: Ziyi lay unable to rise and knocked his head with his hand in thanks for the grace.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi was too ill to rise and could only knock his head with his hand in gratitude for the imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 王解冠珮，以常服傳詔勞問之。

translations.literal: The prince removed cap and girdle ornaments and, in ordinary dress, conveyed the edict to comfort and inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince removed his cap and insignia, changed into ordinary dress, and conveyed the edict of consolation and inquiry.

sentences.zh: 三年，蔡帥李希烈叛，詔哥舒曜討之。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Cai commander Li Xilie rebelled; an edict ordered Geshu Yao to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Li Xilie, the military commissioner of Cai, rebelled, and an edict ordered Geshu Yao to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 八月，希烈自帥眾三萬，圍哥舒曜於襄城，又詔河南都統李勉援之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Xilie personally led thirty thousand troops and besieged Geshu Yao at Xiangcheng; an edict also ordered Li Mian, overall commander of Henan, to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Xilie personally led thirty thousand men and besieged Geshu Yao at Xiangcheng, and Li Mian, overall commander of Henan, was also ordered to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 勉舍襄城，令大將唐漢臣等選勁兵，徑襲許州以解圍。

translations.literal: Mian left Xiangcheng and ordered the great generals Tang Hanchen and others to select crack troops and strike directly at Xuzhou to lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Mian left Xiangcheng and ordered his chief generals Tang Hanchen and others to select crack troops and strike Xuzhou directly in order to lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 漢臣未至許，上遣中使追之，責以違詔，亟旋師，為賊所乘，漢臣之眾大敗。

translations.literal: Before Hanchen reached Xu, the emperor sent a palace envoy to overtake him, rebuked him for disobeying the edict, and ordered him to turn back at once; the rebels seized the opportunity, and Hanchen's force was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Before Hanchen reached Xu, the emperor sent a palace envoy to overtake him, rebuked him for disobeying orders, and ordered an immediate withdrawal; the rebels seized the opportunity, and Hanchen's force was routed.

sentences.zh: 勉恐東都危急，乃分兵數千赴洛，又為賊所隔。

translations.literal: Mian feared the Eastern Capital was in peril and therefore divided several thousand troops to go to Luoyang, but they were again cut off by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that the Eastern Capital was in peril, Mian detached several thousand troops for Luoyang, but they too were cut off by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊眾急攻汴、滑，勉走宋州，朝廷大聳，乃詔誼為揚州大都督，持節荊襄、江西、沔鄂等道節度，兼諸軍行營兵馬元帥，改名誼。

translations.literal: The rebel host pressed attacks on Bian and Hua; Mian fled to Songzhou; the court was greatly alarmed and then ordered Yi as Grand Governor of Yangzhou, with credentials over the Jingxiang, Jiangxi, Mian, E, and other circuit commands, and concurrently supreme commander of all campaign armies; his name was changed to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: As rebel forces pressed their attacks on Bian and Hua, Mian fled to Songzhou. The court was thrown into alarm, and Yi was appointed Grand Governor of Yangzhou with authority over the Jingxiang, Jiangxi, Mian, E, and related circuits, and concurrently supreme commander of all campaign armies; his name was also changed to Yi.

sentences.zh: 又以哥舒翰聲近，士卒竊議，改封普王，令統攝諸軍，進攻希烈。

translations.literal: Also, because Geshu Han sounded similar, the soldiers whispered among themselves; he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Pu and ordered to take overall command of the armies and advance against Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Because the name Geshu Han sounded too similar to another, the troops murmured among themselves, so he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Pu and ordered to take overall command and advance against Xilie.

sentences.zh: 仍以兵部侍郎蕭復為戶部尚書、兼御史大夫、元帥府統軍長史。

translations.literal: Xiao Fu, vice minister of war, was further made minister of revenue, concurrent censor-in-chief, and chief of staff of the supreme commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fu, vice minister of war, was also appointed minister of revenue, concurrent censor-in-chief, and chief of staff at the supreme commander's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 舊例有行軍長史，以復父名衡，特更之。

translations.literal: By old precedent there was a campaign chief of staff; because Fu's father's name was Heng, the title was specially changed.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the post was called campaign chief of staff, but because Fu's father's name was Heng, the title was specially changed.

sentences.zh: 又以新除潭州觀察使孔巢父為右庶子、兼御史大夫，充行軍司馬；

translations.literal: Kong Chaofu, newly appointed observation commissioner of Tanzhou, was made right vice heir apparent, concurrent censor-in-chief, and campaign vice commander;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chaofu, newly appointed observation commissioner of Tanzhou, was made right vice heir apparent, concurrent censor-in-chief, and campaign vice commander.

sentences.zh: 以山南東道節度行軍司馬、檢校兵部郎中、兼御史中丞樊澤為諫議大夫、兼御史中丞、行軍右司馬。

translations.literal: Fan Ze, campaign vice commander of the Shannan East Circuit command, acting director of the war ministry, and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, was made remonstrance official, concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and right campaign vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ze, campaign vice commander of the Shannan East Circuit, acting director of the war ministry, and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, was appointed remonstrance official, concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and right campaign vice commander.

sentences.zh: 刑部員外郎劉從一為吏部郎中、兼中丞；

translations.literal: Liu Congyi, outer vice director of punishments, was made director of the personnel ministry and concurrent vice censor-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congyi, outer vice director of punishments, was appointed director of the personnel ministry and concurrent vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 侍御史韋儹為工部郎中、兼中丞，並充元帥府判官。

translations.literal: Wei Qian, attendant censor, was made director of the works ministry and concurrent vice censor-in-chief; all served as judges on the supreme commander's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qian, attendant censor, was appointed director of the works ministry and concurrent vice censor-in-chief; all served as staff judges at the supreme commander's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 兵部員外郎高參為本司郎中，充元帥府掌書記。

translations.literal: Gao Can, outer vice director of war, was made director of that ministry and served as secretary of the supreme commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Can, outer vice director of war, was promoted to director of that ministry and appointed secretary at the supreme commander's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 以右金吾大將軍渾瑊檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫，為中軍虞候。

translations.literal: Hun Jian, great general of the Right Golden Crow Guard, was made acting minister of works, concurrent censor-in-chief, and middle-army provost marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian, great general of the Right Golden Crow Guard, was appointed acting minister of works, concurrent censor-in-chief, and middle-army provost marshal.

sentences.zh: 江西節度使嗣曹王臯為前軍兵馬使，鄂嶽團練使李兼為之副。

translations.literal: Li Gao, Prince of Cao and military commissioner of Jiangxi, was made front-army commander; Li Jian, regimental commissioner of E and Yue, was his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao, the Prince of Cao and military commissioner of Jiangxi, was appointed front-army commander, with Li Jian, regimental commissioner of E and Yue, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使賈耽為中軍兵馬使。

translations.literal: Jia Dan, military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, was made middle-army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan, military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, was appointed middle-army commander.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使張伯儀充後軍兵馬使。

translations.literal: Zhang Boyi, military commissioner of Jingnan, served as rear-army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Boyi, military commissioner of Jingnan, served as rear-army commander.

sentences.zh: 以左神武軍使王價檢校太子賓客；

translations.literal: Wang Jia, commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, was made acting heir apparent's mentor;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia, commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, was appointed acting heir apparent's mentor.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍高承謙檢校太子詹事；

translations.literal: Gao Chengqian, general of the Left Guard, was made acting heir apparent's household superintendent;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chengqian, general of the Left Guard, was appointed acting heir apparent's household superintendent.

sentences.zh: 前司農少卿郭曙檢校左庶子，前秘書省著作郎常願為秘書少監，並充元帥府押衙。

translations.literal: Guo Shu, former vice minister of agriculture, was made acting left vice heir apparent; Chang Yuan, former compiler in the Secretariat, was made vice director of the Secretariat; all served as headquarters escort officers.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shu, former vice minister of agriculture, was appointed acting left vice heir apparent; Chang Yuan, former compiler in the Secretariat, was made vice director of the Secretariat; all served as headquarters escort officers.

sentences.zh: 制下未行，涇原兵亂而止。

translations.literal: The appointment had been issued but not yet carried out when the Jingyuan troops mutinied and it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The appointments had been issued but not yet carried out when the Jingyuan troops mutinied and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 德宗初聞兵士出怨言，不得賞設，乃令誼與翰林學士姜公輔傳詔安撫，許以厚賞。

translations.literal: When Dezong first heard the soldiers voicing complaints that they had received no rewards or provisions, he ordered Yi and Hanlin academician Jiang Gongfu to convey an edict to reassure them and promised generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong first heard the troops complaining that they had received no rewards or provisions, he ordered Yi and Hanlin academician Jiang Gongfu to convey an edict of reassurance and promised generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 行及內門，兵已陣於闕前；

translations.literal: When they reached the inner gate, the troops had already formed ranks before the palace gate;
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached the inner gate, the troops had already formed ranks before the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 誼狼狽而還，遂奉德宗出幸奉天。

translations.literal: Yi returned in disarray, and then escorted Dezong on the flight to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Yi turned back in disarray, and then escorted Dezong on the flight to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 賊之攻城，誼晝夜傳詔，慰勞諸軍，僅不解帶者月餘。

translations.literal: During the rebels' siege, Yi conveyed edicts day and night to comfort and encourage the armies, going more than a month scarcely ungirding his belt.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebel siege, Yi conveyed edicts day and night to comfort and encourage the armies, going more than a month without so much as loosening his belt.

sentences.zh: 從車駕還宮，復封舒王、開府儀同三司，揚州大都督如故。

translations.literal: When he followed the imperial carriage back to the palace, he was again enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and Kaifu Yitong Sansi, with his post as Grand Governor of Yangzhou unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed the emperor back to the capital, he was again enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and Grand Preceptor with Honorary Credentials Equal to the Three Excellencies, retaining his title as Grand Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年十月薨，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongzhen he died; court audiences were suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of Yongzhen 1 (805), and court audiences were suspended for three days.

sentences.zh: 通王諶，德宗第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Tong Chen, Dezong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Tong Chen was Dezong's third son.

sentences.zh: 大曆十四年封，制授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Dali; by edict appointed Kaifu Yitong Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Dali 14 (779) and appointed Grand Preceptor with Honorary Credentials Equal to the Three Excellencies by edict.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年十月，領宣武軍節度大使、汴宋等州觀察支度營田等使，以宣武都知兵馬使李萬榮為留後，王不出閣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan, he took charge as military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army and observation, supply, and garrison commissioner for Bian, Song, and other prefectures; Li Wanrong, overall commander of Xuanwu forces, was made deputy commissioner; the prince did not leave the mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhenyuan 9 (793), he was named military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army and observation, supply, and garrison commissioner for Bian, Song, and related prefectures; Li Wanrong, overall commander of Xuanwu forces, was appointed deputy commissioner, and the prince did not leave his residence.

sentences.zh: 十一年，河東帥李自良卒，以諶為河東節度大使，以行軍司馬李說知府事，充留後，亦不出閣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the Hedong commander Li Ziliang died; Chen was made military commissioner of Hedong; Li Shuo, campaign vice commander, managed prefectural affairs and served as deputy commissioner; again he did not leave the mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Li Ziliang, commander of Hedong, died; Chen was appointed military commissioner of Hedong, with Li Shuo, campaign vice commander, managing prefectural affairs as deputy commissioner; again the prince did not leave his residence.

sentences.zh: 虔王諒，德宗第四子。

translations.literal: Prince of Qian Liang, Dezong's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qian Liang was Dezong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 大曆十四年封，授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Dali; appointed Kaifu Yitong Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Dali 14 (779) and appointed Grand Preceptor with Honorary Credentials Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，領蔡州節度大使、申光蔡觀察等使，以大將吳少誠為留後。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, he took charge as military commissioner of Caizhou and observation commissioner for Shen, Guang, and Cai; the great general Wu Shaocheng was made deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 (786), he was named military commissioner of Caizhou and observation commissioner for Shen, Guang, and Cai, with the great general Wu Shaocheng as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十年，領朔方靈鹽節度大使、靈州大都督，以朔方行軍司馬李欒為靈府左司馬，知府事，朔方留後。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he took charge as military commissioner of Shuofang, Ling, and Yan and Grand Governor of Lingzhou; Li Luan, campaign vice commander of Shuofang, was made left vice commander of Ling prefecture, managed prefectural affairs, and served as Shuofang deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, he was named military commissioner of Shuofang, Ling, and Yan and Grand Governor of Lingzhou; Li Luan, campaign vice commander of Shuofang, was appointed left vice commander of Ling prefecture, managed prefectural affairs, and served as Shuofang deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年九月，橫海大將程懷信逐其帥懷直。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year, the Henghai great general Cheng Huaixin drove out his commander Huaizhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eleventh year, Cheng Huaixin, a great general of Henghai, drove out his commander Huaizhi.

sentences.zh: 十月，以諒領橫海節度大使、滄景觀察等使，以都知兵馬使程懷信為留後，王不出閣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Liang was made military commissioner of Henghai and observation commissioner for Cang and Jing; Cheng Huaixin, overall commander of forces, was made deputy commissioner; the prince did not leave the mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Liang was appointed military commissioner of Henghai and observation commissioner for Cang and Jing; Cheng Huaixin, overall commander of forces, was made deputy commissioner, and the prince did not leave his residence.

sentences.zh: 十六年，徐帥張建封卒，徐軍亂，又以諒領徐州節度大使、徐泗濠觀察處置等使，以建封子愔為留後。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Xu commander Zhang Jianfeng died and the Xu army mutinied; Liang was again made military commissioner of Xuzhou and observation and disposition commissioner for Xu, Si, and Hao; Jianfeng's son Yin was made deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Zhang Jianfeng, commander of Xu, died and the Xu army mutinied; Liang was again appointed military commissioner of Xuzhou and observation and disposition commissioner for Xu, Si, and Hao, with Jianfeng's son Yin as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 肅王詳，德宗第五子。

translations.literal: Prince of Su Xiang, Dezong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Su Xiang was Dezong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 大曆十四年六月封。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed in the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the sixth month of Dali 14 (779).

sentences.zh: 建中三年十月薨，時年四歲，廢朝三日，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Jianzhong he died, aged four; court audiences were suspended for three days; posthumously made Grand Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of Jianzhong 3 (782), aged four; court audiences were suspended for three days, and he was posthumously made Grand Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 性聰惠，上尤憐之，追念無已，不令起墳墓，詔如西域法，議層磚造塔。

translations.literal: By nature clever and gifted, the emperor especially favored him; his grief was unending; he would not permit a tomb mound to be raised and ordered that, according to Western Regions practice, a pagoda of stacked bricks be considered.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and quick-witted, he was especially beloved by the emperor, whose grief knew no end. Dezong would not permit a tomb mound and ordered that, following Western Regions practice, a pagoda of stacked bricks be built instead.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使判官、司門郎中李巖上言曰：「墳墓之義，經典有常，自古至今，無聞異制。

translations.literal: Li Yan, judge under the commissioner of rites and director of the gate ministry, submitted a memorial saying: "The meaning of tombs and graves is fixed in the classics; from antiquity to the present, no different system has been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, judge under the commissioner of rites and director of the gate ministry, submitted a memorial saying, "The meaning of tombs and graves is fixed in the classics. From antiquity to the present, no different system has ever been heard of.

sentences.zh: 層磚起塔，始於天竺，名曰『浮圖』，行之中華，竊恐非禮。

translations.literal: Raising a pagoda of stacked bricks began in Tianzhu and is called a 'stupa'; its practice in the Central Realm, I fear privately, is not in accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Raising a pagoda of stacked bricks began in India, where it is called a stupa. To practice it in the Central Realm, I fear, would not accord with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 況肅王天屬，名位尊崇，喪葬之儀，存乎簡冊，舉而不法，垂訓非輕。

translations.literal: Moreover, Prince of Su is of heaven's kin and his name and rank are exalted; funeral rites are preserved in the written records—if what is done is not lawful, the instruction handed down will not be light.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Prince of Su was of the imperial blood and held an exalted rank. Funeral rites are preserved in the written records. To act contrary to them would set a precedent of no small weight.

sentences.zh: 伏請準令造墳，庶遵典禮。」

translations.literal: I humbly request that a tomb be made according to statute, so that canonical ritual may be followed."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly request that a tomb be made according to statute, so that canonical ritual may be followed."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 文敬太子謜，順宗之子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenjing Song, Shunzong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenjing Song was the son of Shunzong.

sentences.zh: 德宗愛之，命為子。

translations.literal: Dezong loved him and ordered him to be made his son.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong loved him and adopted him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，封邕王，授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, enfeoffed as Prince of Yong; appointed Kaifu Yitong Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 4 (788), he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong and appointed Grand Preceptor with Honorary Credentials Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 七年，定州張孝忠卒，以謜領義武軍節度大使、易定觀察等使，以定州刺史張茂昭為留後。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Zhang Xiaozhong of Dingzhou died; Song was made military commissioner of the Yiwu Army and observation commissioner for Yi and Ding; Zhang Maozhao, prefect of Dingzhou, was made deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Zhang Xiaozhong of Dingzhou died; Song was appointed military commissioner of the Yiwu Army and observation commissioner for Yi and Ding, with Zhang Maozhao, prefect of Dingzhou, as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十年六月，潞帥李抱真卒，又以謜領昭義節度大使、澤潞邢洺名磁觀察等使，以潞將王虔休為潞府司馬、知留後。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year, the Lu commander Li Baozhen died; Song was again made military commissioner of Zhaoyi and observation commissioner for Ze, Lu, Xing, Ming, Ci, and other prefectures; the Lu general Wang Qianxiu was made Lu prefecture vice commander and acting deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the tenth year, Li Baozhen, commander of Lu, died; Song was again appointed military commissioner of Zhaoyi and observation commissioner for Ze, Lu, Xing, Ming, Ci, and related prefectures, with the Lu general Wang Qianxiu as Lu prefecture vice commander and acting deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十五年十月薨，時年十八，廢朝三日，贈文敬太子，所司備禮冊命。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifteenth year he died, aged eighteen; court audiences were suspended for three days; posthumously made Crown Prince Wenjing; the relevant offices prepared ritual investiture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the fifteenth year, aged eighteen; court audiences were suspended for three days; he was posthumously made Crown Prince Wenjing, and the relevant offices prepared the ritual investiture.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，葬於昭應，有陵無號。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he was buried at Zhaoying; there was a mausoleum but no posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year he was buried at Zhaoying; he had a mausoleum but no posthumous temple name.

sentences.zh: 發引之日，百官送於通化門外，列位哭送。

translations.literal: On the day the procession set out, the hundred officials escorted him outside Tonghua Gate, standing in ranks and weeping as they sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the funeral procession set out, officials of all ranks escorted him outside Tonghua Gate, standing in ranks and weeping as they sent him off.

sentences.zh: 是日風雪寒甚，近歲未有。

translations.literal: That day the wind and snow were bitterly cold, such as had not been seen in recent years.
translations.idiomatic: That day brought wind and snow of exceptional bitterness, such as had not been seen in recent years.

sentences.zh: 詔置陵署令丞。

translations.literal: An edict established director and vice director for the mausoleum office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict established director and vice director posts for the mausoleum office.

sentences.zh: 資王謙，德宗第七子。

translations.literal: Prince of Zi Qian, Dezong's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zi Qian was Dezong's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 大曆十四年封。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Dali 14 (779).

sentences.zh: 代王諲，德宗第八子。

translations.literal: Prince of Dai Jin, Dezong's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Dai Jin was Dezong's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 本封縉雲郡王，早薨。

translations.literal: Originally enfeoffed as Prince of Jinyun commandery; died early.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been enfeoffed as Prince of Jinyun commandery and died young.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，追封代王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 2 (781), he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 昭王誡，德宗第九子。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Jie, Dezong's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Jie was Dezong's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年封。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed in the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Zhenyuan 21 (805).

sentences.zh: 欽王諤，德宗第十子。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin E, Dezong's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin E was Dezong's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，詔曰：「王者之制，子弟畢封，所以固籓輔而重社稷，古今之通義也。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, an edict said: "The institution of kings is that younger brothers and sons are all enfeoffed, thereby to secure the feudal support and give weight to the altars of soil and grain—this is the universal principle of antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong took the throne, an edict said, "The institution of kings is that all younger brothers and sons receive fiefs, thereby securing the feudal support and giving weight to the altars of soil and grain. This is the universal principle of antiquity and the present.

sentences.zh: 第十弟諤等，寬簡忠厚，生知孝敬，行皆由禮，誌不違仁。

translations.literal: The tenth younger brother E and the others are generous, simple, and loyal and honest; filial respect is inborn in them; their conduct is all guided by ritual; their intent does not depart from benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: My tenth younger brother E and the others are generous, simple, loyal, and honest. Filial respect comes naturally to them. Their conduct is guided by ritual, and their intent never strays from benevolence.

sentences.zh: 樂善本於性情，好賢宗於師傅。

translations.literal: Delight in goodness is rooted in their nature and disposition; love of worth they take from their teachers and tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Their delight in goodness springs from their nature, and their love of worth they learned from their teachers and tutors.

sentences.zh: 纘修六藝，達人倫風化之源；

translations.literal: They continue and cultivate the Six Arts and comprehend the source of human relations and transforming instruction;
translations.idiomatic: They continue and cultivate the Six Arts and comprehend the source of human relations and civilizing instruction.

sentences.zh: 博習群言，知惠和睦友之道。

translations.literal: They study broadly the many teachings and know the Way of kindness, harmony, and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: They study broadly the many teachings and understand the way of kindness, harmony, and friendship.

sentences.zh: 溫恭朝夕，允茂厥猷，克有嘉聞，宜封土宇。

translations.literal: Warm and respectful morning and evening, they truly flourish in their plans, and can achieve fine repute; they should be enfeoffed with territory.
translations.idiomatic: Warm and respectful from morning to evening, they truly flourish in their conduct and have earned fine repute. It is fitting that they receive territorial enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 諤可封欽王。

translations.literal: E may be enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: E is to be enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 第十一弟可封珍王。」

translations.literal: The eleventh younger brother may be enfeoffed as Prince of Zhen."
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh younger brother is to be enfeoffed as Prince of Zhen."

sentences.zh: 珍王諴，德宗第十一子，與欽王同制封。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhen Kan, Dezong's eleventh son, enfeoffed by the same edict as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhen Kan was Dezong's eleventh son and was enfeoffed by the same edict as Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 德宗仁孝，動循法度，雖子弟姑妹之親，無所假借。

translations.literal: Dezong was benevolent and filial and in action followed statutes; even with kin such as sons, younger brothers, aunts, and sisters, he made no exceptions.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was benevolent and filial and in all his actions followed the law. Even toward sons, younger brothers, aunts, and sisters, he made no exceptions.

sentences.zh: 建中初，詔親王子弟帶開府朝秩者，出就本班。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, an edict ordered imperial sons and younger brothers who bore Kaifu court rank to go out and take their proper places in the original ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianzhong, an edict ordered imperial sons and younger brothers who held Grand Preceptor court rank to take their proper places in the regular ranks.

sentences.zh: 又以公主、郡縣主出降，與舅姑抗禮。

translations.literal: Also, because princesses and commandery and county princesses married down and stood on equal ritual footing with parents-in-law,
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed the fact that when princesses and commandery and county princesses married, they stood on equal ritual footing with their parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「冠婚之義，人倫大經。

translations.literal: an edict said: "The meaning of capping and marriage is the great constant of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The meaning of capping and marriage is the great constant of human relations.

sentences.zh: 昔唐堯降嬪，帝乙歸妹。

translations.literal: In antiquity Tang Yao sent down a consort; Di Yi returned his younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, Tang Yao sent down a consort in marriage, and Di Yi gave his younger sister in marriage.

sentences.zh: 迨於漢氏，同姓主之。

translations.literal: Down to the Han house, those of the same surname were lords over them.
translations.idiomatic: By the Han dynasty, those of the same surname took precedence.

sentences.zh: 爰自近古，禮教陵夷，公郡法度，僭差殊制。

translations.literal: From recent antiquity, ritual teaching declined; ducal and commandery regulations and statutes diverged in usurping excess and irregular systems.
translations.idiomatic: From recent antiquity onward, ritual teaching declined, and ducal and commandery regulations diverged into irregular and excessive practices.

sentences.zh: 姻族闕齒序之義，舅姑有拜下之禮，自家刑國，多愧古人。

translations.literal: Marriage kin lacked the meaning of seniority order; parents-in-law had the ritual of bowing down—from regulating the family to punishing the state, much shamed the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage kin lacked proper seniority, and parents-in-law were made to perform bowing rituals. From family regulation to state governance, much of this shamed the ancients.

sentences.zh: 今縣主有行，將俟嘉令，俾親執棗栗，以見舅姑；

translations.literal: Now the county princesses are about to depart; they will await the fine command, so that in person they may hold dates and chestnuts to meet their parents-in-law;
translations.idiomatic: Now that the county princesses are about to marry, they shall await the proper command so that they may personally present dates and chestnuts when meeting their parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 敬遵宗婦之儀，降就家人之禮。

translations.literal: Reverently follow the ritual of a clan daughter-in-law and descend to take up the rites of a family member.
translations.idiomatic: They shall reverently follow the ritual of a clan daughter-in-law and descend to the rites owed within the family.

sentences.zh: 事資變革，以抑浮華。

translations.literal: The matter requires reform in order to restrain empty show.
translations.idiomatic: This matter requires reform in order to restrain empty display.

sentences.zh: 其令禮儀使與禮官博士，約古今舊儀及《開元禮》，詳定公主、郡縣主出降、覿見之文儀以聞。」

translations.literal: Let the commissioner of rites and the ritual officials and erudites, drawing on ancient and modern old rites and the Kaiyuan Rites, work out in detail the written rites for princesses and commandery and county princesses marrying down and for presentation audiences, and report them."
translations.idiomatic: Let the commissioner of rites and the ritual officials and erudites, drawing on ancient and modern precedents and the Kaiyuan Rites, work out in detail the written rites for princesses and commandery and county princesses marrying down and for presentation audiences, and report them."

sentences.zh: 初，開元中置禮會院於崇仁裏。

translations.literal: At first, in the Kaiyuan era a Rites Assembly Court was established in Chongren Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Kaiyuan era, a Rites Assembly Court had been established in Chongren Lane.

sentences.zh: 自兵興已來，廢而不修，故公、郡、縣主不時降嫁，殆三十年，至有華發而猶丱者，雖居內館，而不獲覲見十六年矣。

translations.literal: Since the armies were raised it had been abandoned and not restored; therefore ducal, commandery, and county princesses did not marry down in season for nearly thirty years, until some with gray hair were still in childhood coiffure; though they dwelt in the inner lodges, they had not been granted audience for sixteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Since the armies were raised it had fallen into disuse, so ducal, commandery, and county princesses went unmarried for nearly thirty years. Some with gray hair still wore childhood coiffure, and though they lived in the inner lodges, they had not been granted audience for sixteen years.

sentences.zh: 凡皇族子弟，皆散棄無位，或流落他縣，湮沈不齒錄，無異匹庶。

translations.literal: All imperial clan sons and younger brothers were scattered and abandoned without posts, or drifted to other prefectures, sunk and not entered in registers, no different from commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen were scattered and left without posts, or drifted to other prefectures, sunk into obscurity and omitted from the registers, no different from commoners.

sentences.zh: 及德宗即位，敘用枝屬，以時婚嫁，公族老幼，莫不悲感。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, he arranged employment for branch kin and timely marriages; the ducal clan, old and young, none failed to be moved to grief and gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong took the throne, he arranged employment for branch kin and timely marriages. The ducal clan, old and young alike, were moved to tears of grief and gratitude.

sentences.zh: 初即位，將謁太廟，始與公、郡、縣主相見於大次中，尊者展其敬，幼者申其愛，歔欷哭泣之聲聞於朝，公卿陪列者為之淒然。

translations.literal: Shortly after taking the throne, when he was about to visit the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he first met the ducal, commandery, and county princesses in the great side hall; the elders displayed their respect, the young expressed their affection; sounds of sobbing and weeping were heard in court, and the dukes and ministers standing in attendance were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after his accession, as he was about to visit the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he first met the ducal, commandery, and county princesses in the great side hall. The elders displayed their respect and the young expressed their affection. Sobbing and weeping were heard throughout the court, and the dukes and ministers in attendance were moved to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 每將有大禮，必與諸父昆弟同其齋次。

translations.literal: Whenever a great rite was impending, he invariably shared the fasting quarters with his uncles and brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a great state rite was impending, he invariably shared the fasting quarters with his uncles and brothers.

sentences.zh: 及岳陽、信寧、宜芳、永順、朗陵、陽安、襄城、德清、南華、元城、新鄉等十一縣主同月出降，敕所司大小之物，必周其用。

translations.literal: When the eleven county princesses of Yueyang, Xinning, Yifang, Yongshun, Langling, Yang'an, Xiangcheng, Deqing, Nanhua, Yuancheng, and Xinxiang married down in the same month, an edict ordered the relevant offices that great and small items must fully meet their needs.
translations.idiomatic: When the eleven county princesses of Yueyang, Xinning, Yifang, Yongshun, Langling, Yang'an, Xiangcheng, Deqing, Nanhua, Yuancheng, and Xinxiang married down in the same month, an edict ordered the relevant offices to supply everything needed, great and small alike.

sentences.zh: 至於櫛、纚、笄、總，皆經於心，各給錢三百萬，使中官主之，以買田業，不得侈用。

translations.literal: As for combs, silk threads, hairpins, and coiled hair, all passed through his mind; each was given three million cash, with palace eunuchs placed in charge to buy fields and estates, and extravagant use was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Even combs, silk threads, hairpins, and coiled hair received his personal attention. Each princess was given three million cash, with palace eunuchs placed in charge to buy fields and estates, and extravagant spending was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 其衣服之飾，使內司計造，不在此數。

translations.literal: Their clothing and ornaments were ordered calculated and made by the inner service; these were not included in that sum.
translations.idiomatic: Their clothing and ornaments were ordered calculated and made by the inner service and were not included in that sum.

sentences.zh: 是時所司度人用一籠花，計錢七十萬。

translations.literal: At that time the relevant offices estimated that one cage of flowers per person would cost seven hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the relevant offices estimated that one cage of flowers per person would cost seven hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「籠花首飾，婦禮不可闕，然用費太廣，即無謂也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Cage flowers as head ornaments are a woman's rite that cannot be omitted, yet if the expense is too great, it is meaningless.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Cage flowers as head ornaments are a woman's rite that cannot be omitted, yet if the expense is too great, it is meaningless.

sentences.zh: 宜損之又損之。」

translations.literal: It should be reduced again and again."
translations.idiomatic: It should be reduced again and again."

sentences.zh: 及三萬而止。

translations.literal: It was stopped at thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The cost was finally set at thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 帝謂主等曰：「吾非有所愛，但不欲無益之費耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the princesses and others: "It is not that I have any partiality, but only that I do not wish useless expense."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the princesses, "It is not that I favor one over another. I simply do not wish useless expense."

sentences.zh: 各以余錢六十萬賜之，以備他用。

translations.literal: Each was given the remaining six hundred thousand cash for other uses.
translations.idiomatic: Each was then given the remaining six hundred thousand cash for other uses.

sentences.zh: 舊例，皇姬下嫁，舅姑返拜而婦不答。

translations.literal: By old precedent, when an imperial daughter married down, the parents-in-law returned the bow while the wife did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: By old precedent, when an imperial daughter married down, the parents-in-law returned the bow while the wife did not respond.

sentences.zh: 及是制下，禮官定制曰：「既成婚於禮會院，明晨，舅坐於堂東階西向，姑南向，婦執笄，盛以棗栗，升自西階，再拜，跪奠於舅席前。

translations.literal: When this regulation was issued, the ritual officials fixed the rites, saying: "After the marriage is completed at the Rites Assembly Court, the next morning the father-in-law sits on the eastern steps of the hall facing west, the mother-in-law faces south, the wife holds the hairpin, filled with dates and chestnuts, ascends by the western steps, bows twice, kneels and presents before the father-in-law's mat.
translations.idiomatic: When this regulation was issued, the ritual officials fixed the rites, saying, "After the marriage is completed at the Rites Assembly Court, the next morning the father-in-law sits on the eastern steps of the hall facing west and the mother-in-law faces south. The wife holds the hairpin filled with dates and chestnuts, ascends by the western steps, bows twice, and kneels to present it before the father-in-law's mat.

sentences.zh: 退降受胙，盛以腶修。

translations.literal: She withdraws, descends, and receives the sacrificial meat, placed in dried meat strips.
translations.idiomatic: She withdraws, descends, and receives the sacrificial meat placed in dried meat strips.

sentences.zh: 升，北面再拜，跪奠於姑席前。

translations.literal: She ascends, faces north and bows twice, kneels and presents before the mother-in-law's mat.
translations.idiomatic: She ascends, faces north, bows twice, and kneels to present it before the mother-in-law's mat.

sentences.zh: 降，東面拜婿之伯叔兄弟姊妹。

translations.literal: She descends and, facing east, bows to the husband's uncles, brothers, and sisters.
translations.idiomatic: She descends and, facing east, bows to the husband's uncles, brothers, and sisters.

sentences.zh: 已而謝恩於光順門，婿之親族亦隨之，然後會宴於十六宅。」

translations.literal: Then she gives thanks for grace at Guangshun Gate, the husband's kin also follow, and afterward a banquet is held at the Sixteen Mansions."
translations.idiomatic: She then gives thanks at Guangshun Gate, followed by the husband's kin, and afterward a banquet is held at the Sixteen Mansions."

sentences.zh: 是日，縣主皆如其制。

translations.literal: That day, all the county princesses followed this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: That day, all the county princesses followed this regulation.

sentences.zh: 初，贈司徒沈易良之妻崔氏，即太后之季父母也，帝每見之，方屣而靴，召王、韋二美人出拜。

translations.literal: At first, Lady Cui, wife of the posthumously made Minister of Works Shen Yiliang, was the empress dowager's youngest aunt and uncle; whenever the emperor saw her, he was just slipping on his shoes and putting on his boots and summoned the two beauties Wang and Wei to come out and bow.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui, wife of the posthumously made Minister of Works Shen Yiliang, was the empress dowager's youngest aunt and uncle. Whenever the emperor saw her, he was still slipping on his shoes and boots and would summon the two beauties Wang and Wei to come out and bow.

sentences.zh: 敕崔氏坐受勿答。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lady Cui to sit and receive the bow without returning it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Lady Cui to sit and receive the bow without returning it.

sentences.zh: 故戚屬之間，罔不憚其敬，不肅而遵禮法焉。

translations.literal: Therefore among affinal kin none failed to fear his reverence, and without severity they followed ritual law.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore among affinal kin none failed to respect his authority, and without harshness they followed ritual law.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：夫聖人君臨宇縣，肇啟邦基，莫不受命上玄，膺名帝箓。

translations.literal: [Discussion] The historiographer says: The sage rules the realm under heaven and first opens the foundation of the state; none fails to receive mandate from the Supreme Mystery and bear the name on the imperial register.
translations.idiomatic: [Discussion] The historiographer writes: The sage who rules all under heaven and lays the foundation of the state invariably receives his mandate from Heaven and bears his name on the imperial register.

sentences.zh: 自太昊已降，五運相推，迄於殷湯，歷數綿永。

translations.literal: From Taihao downward, the five cycles succeeded one another; down to Tang of Yin, the dynastic span was long and enduring.

sentences.zh: 但設均平之化，未聞封建之名。

translations.literal: They only established the transforming influence of equal balance; the name of enfeoffment was not heard of.

sentences.zh: 洎乎周、漢，始以子弟建侯樹屏，以作維城。

translations.literal: Down to Zhou and Han, they first used sons and younger brothers to establish lords and plant screens, thereby making bulwark cities.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhou and Han dynasties, sons and younger brothers were first enfeoffed as lords to serve as bulwarks of the realm.

sentences.zh: 及王室浸微，遂有莽、卓之亂。

translations.literal: When the royal house gradually declined, there followed the disorders of Mang and Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 唐室自艱難已後，兩河兵革屢興，諸王雖封，竟不出閣，夫帝王居寰宇之尊，撫億兆之眾，但能平一理道，夙夜嚴恭，任賢使能，設官分職，自然四海樂推。

translations.literal: Since the Tang house's time of hardship, military campaigns in the two He regions arose repeatedly; though the princes were enfeoffed, in the end they did not leave their mansions. The Son of Heaven occupies the honor of all within the four seas and nurtures the masses in the hundreds of millions—if he can unify and rectify the Way, be vigilant morning and night, employ the worthy and use the capable, establish offices and divide duties, naturally the four seas will gladly acclaim him.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tang dynasty's time of hardship, warfare in the two He regions arose repeatedly. Though the princes received fiefs, in the end they never left their residences. The emperor occupies the highest honor under heaven and governs the masses in the hundreds of millions. If he can unify and rectify the Way, remain vigilant morning and night, employ the worthy and use the capable, and establish offices with divided duties, the four seas will naturally acclaim him.

sentences.zh: 天命所祐，縱無封建，亦鴻基永固，安俟嬰孺鎮重哉？

translations.literal: Protected by Heaven's mandate, even without enfeoffment the great foundation is forever secure—why wait for infants and children to hold weighty posts?
translations.idiomatic: Protected by Heaven's mandate, even without enfeoffment the great foundation remains forever secure. Why must one wait for infants and children to hold weighty posts?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孝文秉禮，道弘籓邸。

translations.literal: Praise says: Xiaowen upheld ritual; the Way was spread in the princely mansions.

translations.idiomatic: Yet like caged birds of ill omen, in the end they knew only enclosure and restraint.
